title: Inversion and Emphasis / Inversión na ịgụ na ịtụlite
bridge: Na English, tụọnụ na ịtụlite dị ka ndị Igbo na-eme ka okwu dị mma, mana n'okpuru English, ịtụlite na-eme ka okwu dị mma na-achọrọ ịgbanwe mgbochi nke ndị a na-akpọ 'subject-verb' ma ọ bụ na-eme n'ụzọ dị iche iche dị ka 'not only... but also' ma ọ bụ 'so + adjective... that'. Ndị a na-eme ka okpuru English dị iche na ndị Igbo nke na-akpọ Spanish nwere ike ịdị iche na-achọrọ ịtụlite, nke a na-eme ka ndị Igbo na-akpọ Spanish na-achọrọ ịtụlite n'okpuru okwu na-eme ka okwu dị mma. Ọ bụrụ na ị na-eme okwu n'okpuru English, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite mgbochi nke ndị a, n'ihi na ị na-eme okwu n'okpuru Spanish, ị ga-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche. N'ihi ndị a, ọtụtụ ndị Igbo na-akpọ Spanish na-eme okwu n'ụzọ ọma, mana n'okpuru English, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite mgbochi nke ndị a. N'ihi ndị a, ọtụtụ ndị Igbo na-akpọ Spanish na-eme okwu n'ụzọ ọma, mana n'okpuru English, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite mgbochi nke ndị a.
rule: Ịtụlite na English na-eme ka okwu dị mma ma ọ bụ na ụzọ dị iche nke na-eme ka okwu dị mma. Ọ na-eme n'ụzọ ndị a: 1) Mgbe ndị adverb nwere ihe ọma ma ọ bụ nke ọma n'ụzọ dị iche, dị ka 'never', 'rarely', 'seldom', 'hardly', 'scarcely', 'no sooner', 'not only', 'not until', 'little', 'in no way'. N'ụzọ ndị a, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite nke auxiliary (do/does/did, have/has, will, etc.) na-akwado n'elu nke subject, na-eme ka nke verb na-akpọ infinitive n'ọnụ ọgụgụ 'to'. N'ịkpọ: 'Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.' 2) Na-akpọ 'so + adjective/adverb' na 'such + noun' n'isi okwu na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche, na-akpọ 'that' (n'ihi na 'that' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche): 'So beautiful was the painting that everyone stared.' 3) Iji tinyere n'ụzọ dị iche na-akpọ 'not only... but also', 'only after', 'only if', etc. 4) Na ụzọ ndị a na-akpọ conditional nke na-eme ka okwu dị mma, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite nke subject na nke verb n'okpuru 'if' na-eme ka okwu dị mma: 'Had I known, I would have come.' 5) Na-akpọ 'here' na 'there' mgbe nke verb na-akpọ intransitive na nke subject na-akpọ noun, a na-akpọ pronoun. 6) Na ụzọ ndị a na-akpọ wish nke na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'akpọ 'may' (nke na-eme ka okwu dị mma). N'ihi ndị a, na English, ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okwu ndepụta (n'ihi na na Spanish n'okpuru okwu ndepụta dị iche n'okwu ndepụta ma ọ bụ n'okwu ndepụta), mana ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite mgbochi nke ndị a. ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite mgbochi nke ndị a n'okpuru adverb nwere ihe ọma, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite nke auxiliary, n'ihi na verbs nke na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okwu ndepụta.

concept_examples.text: Never have I encountered such a challenging problem.
concept_examples.translation: A na-emeri m ike ịhụ nsogbu dị ọtọ na-enweghị ike.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈnɛvər hæv aɪ ɪnˈkaʊntərd sʌtʃ ə ˈtʃælɪndʒɪŋ ˈprɒbləm/

concept_examples.text: Not only did she lose her job, but she also had to relocate.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-egbu ụlọ ọrụ ya, ọ ga-eme ka ọ na-agafe.
concept_examples.phonetic: /nɒt ˈəʊnli dɪd ʃiː luːz hɜː dʒɒb bʌt ʃiː ˈɔːlsəʊ hæd tə ˌriːləʊˈkeɪt/

concept_examples.text: So intense was the heat that the roads began to melt.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ dị mma na-akpọ nke ọnwụ dị iche n'ihi na ndoro ndoro nke ụzọ na-eme ka ha na-egbu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /səʊ ɪnˈtens wɒz ðə hiːt ðæt ðə rəʊdz bɪˈɡæn tə melt/

concept_examples.text: Only after the war did the country experience true reconstruction.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-egbu ugwu, ndị a ga-eme ka ụwa na-achọrọ ịmụta nke ọma.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈəʊnli ˈæftə ðə wɔː dɪd ðə ˈkʌntri ɪkˈspɪəriəns truː ˌriːkənˈstrʌkʃən/

common_error.wrong: Not only he has a beautiful voice, but also he sings well.
common_error.correct: Not only does he have a beautiful voice, but he also sings well.
common_error.correct_alt: Not only does he have a beautiful voice, but he also sings well.
common_error.explanation: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-eme okwu n'okpuru Spanish, ị ga-eme ka okwu dị ka 'No solo él tiene una voz hermosa, sino que además canta bien', na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche. Mana n'okpuru English, mgbe ị na-eme okwu na-akpọ 'not only', ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite nke auxiliary na nke subject. Ọ bụrụ na ị na-eme okwu n'ụzọ dị iche, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite nke auxiliary 'does' n'okpuru present simple, n'ihi na nke verb na-akpọ 'have' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche. Ọ bụrụ na ị na-eme okwu n'ụzọ dị iche, ị ga-achọrọ ịtụlite nke auxiliary n'okpuru 'not only', 'never', 'rarely', etc., nke ụzọ bụ: auxiliary + subject + verb.

examples.original: Never have I seen such a dedicated team.
examples.phonetic: /ˈnɛvər hæv aɪ siːn sʌtʃ ə ˈdɛdɪkeɪtɪd tiːm/
examples.translation: A na-emeri m ike ịhụ ndị a na-akpọ 'never' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'have' na-akpọ 'I'. N'okpuru Spanish, ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche, mana ị na-eme ka okwu dị ka 'Nunca he visto'.
examples.note: N'okpuru 'never', ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'have' na-akpọ 'I'.

examples.original: Rarely do we find such an honest politician.
examples.phonetic: /ˈreəli duː wiː faɪnd sʌtʃ ən ˈɒnɪst ˌpɒlɪˈtɪʃən/
examples.translation: Ọ dị mma na-akpọ ndị a na-akpọ 'rarely', ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'do' na-akpọ auxiliary n'okpuru present simple, na nke verb na-akpọ 'find' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche.
examples.note: Con 'rarely', se usa 'do' como auxiliar en presente simple, y el verbo 'find' permanece en infinitivo.

examples.original: Hardly had we left the house when it started to rain.
examples.phonetic: /ˈhɑːdli hæd wiː lɛft ðə haʊs wɛn ɪt ˈstɑːtɪd tə reɪn/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na a na-egbu ụlọ anya mgbe anyị na-egbu ụlọ anya, ọ ga-eme ka mmiri na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'hardly... when'.
examples.note: La estructura 'hardly... when' indica que algo ocurrió inmediatamente después de otra cosa. Se usa pasado perfecto con inversión.

examples.original: So tired was she that she fell asleep instantly.
examples.phonetic: /səʊ ˈtaɪəd wɒz ʃiː ðæt ʃiː fɛl əˈsliːp ˈɪnstəntli/
examples.translation: Ọ dị mma na-akpọ ndị a na-akpọ 'so' na 'such', ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'so + adjective + was/were + subject + that' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'tan... na'.
examples.note: N'okpuru 'so + adjective', ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'was/were' na-akpọ subject.

examples.original: Such was the noise that nobody could sleep.
examples.phonetic: /sʌtʃ wɒz ðə nɔɪz ðæt ˈnəʊbədi kʊd sliːp/
examples.translation: Ọ dị mma na-akpọ ndị a na-akpọ 'such' n'isi okwu na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche. N'ihi ndị a, 'such' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'adjective', na nke verb 'was' na-akpọ subject.
examples.note: Se usa 'such' seguido de un sustantivo al inicio para dar énfasis. Aquí, 'such' cumple la función de adjetivo, y el verbo 'was' precede al sujeto.

examples.original: So quickly did she finish that everyone was amazed.
examples.phonetic: /səʊ ˈkwɪkli dɪd ʃiː ˈfɪnɪʃ ðæt ˈɛvrɪwʌn wɒz əˈmeɪzd/
examples.translation: Ọ dị mma na-akpọ ndị a na-akpọ 'so' na 'quickly', ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'did' na-akpọ auxiliary na nke verb na-akpọ infinitive.
examples.note: Cuando se usa un adverbio ('quickly') en lugar de un adjetivo, se necesita el auxiliar 'did' con el verbo principal en infinitivo.

levels.label: Conditional Inversion and Formal Structures
levels.translation: Ịtụlite nke conditional na ụzọ dị iche

examples.original: Had I known about the delay, I would have left earlier.
examples.phonetic: /hæd aɪ nəʊn əˈbaʊt ðə dɪˈleɪ aɪ wʊd hæv lɛft ˈɜːliə/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na m na-akwụ ọnụ maka nkwụ ụlọ, m ga-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'if' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'had'.
examples.note: N'okpuru conditional nke na-eme ka okwu dị mma, ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'if' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'had'.

examples.original: Should you need any assistance, do not hesitate to call us.
examples.phonetic: /ʃʊd juː niːd ˈɛni əˈsɪstəns duː nɒt ˈhɛzɪteɪt tə kɔːl ʌs/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-achọ ịrịbaụ nke ọ bụla, ị ga-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'should' n'ihi na ụzọ dị iche nke na-eme ka okwu dị mma. N'okpuru Spanish, ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'si necesitara'.
examples.note: N'okpuru 'should', ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'if' na-eme ka okwu dị mma.

examples.original: No sooner had the concert started than the fire alarm went off.
examples.phonetic: /nəʊ ˈsuːnə hæd ðə ˈkɒnsət ˈstɑːtɪd ðæn ðə ˈfaɪər əˈlɑːm wɛnt ɒf/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-egbu ugwu mgbe ọ na-egbu ugwu, ọ ga-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'no sooner... than' na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'past perfect'.
examples.note: 'No sooner... than' indica que una cosa ocurrió inmediatamente después de otra, con inversión en pasado perfecto.

examples.original: Were the government to propose such a law, it would be highly controversial.
examples.phonetic: /wɜː ðə ˈɡʌvənmənt tə prəˈpəʊz sʌtʃ ə lɔː ɪt wʊd biː ˈhaɪli ˌkɒntrəˈvɜːʃəl/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ụlọ ọrụ na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'were + subject + to + infinitive' n'ihi na 'if + past simple'.
examples.note: N'okpuru 'were + subject + to + infinitive', ị na-eme ka okwu dị mma n'ụzọ dị iche n'okpuru 'if + past simple'.

translations.ig: Nkọwa ọtụtụ na ụzọ dị iche

title: Register and Style: Formal, Informal, and Neutral / Nkọwa na Ntughari: Mmadụ, Oru na Nke Na-akpụkpere
bridge: N'azịị Igbo, nkọwa na-egosi na usoro dị iche iche na usoro ụtọ, ma ọ bụ naanị na nkọwa ụtọ na nkọwa ọma. N'ụdị ahịa, nkọwa na-egosi na usoro dị iche iche na usoro ụtọ, ma ọ bụ naanị na nkọwa ụtọ na nkọwa ọma. N'ụdị ahịa, nkọwa na-egosi na usoro dị iche iche na usoro ụtọ, ma ọ bụ naanị na nkọwa ụtọ na nkọwa ọma. N'ụdị ahịa, nkọwa na-egosi na usoro dị iche iche na usoro ụtọ, ma ọ bụ naanị na nkọwa ụtọ na nkọwa ọma.

concept_examples.text: I would be grateful if you could provide me with further details.
concept_examples.translation: A ga-emeri m unu ike ịmalite ịnwale ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd biː ˈɡreɪtfʊl ɪf juː kʊd prəˈvaɪd miː wɪð ˈfɜːðər ˈdiːteɪlz/

concept_examples.text: Could you send me the report by Friday?
concept_examples.translation: Ụnọọkwu ndoro ndoro ga-esi n'ụbọchị mbụ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː sɛnd miː ðə rɪˈpɔːrt baɪ ˈfraɪdeɪ/

concept_examples.text: No worries, I'll get back to you later.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ dịghị n'ike, m ga-emeri gị n'oge ọzọ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /nəʊ ˈwʌriz aɪl ɡɛt bæk tə juː ˈleɪtər/

common_error.wrong: I am writing this in order to ask you for a favor, because I need to know if you can help me with the presentation.
common_error.correct: I'm writing to ask a favor – could you help me with the presentation?
common_error.correct_alt: I'm writing to ask you a favor: would you be able to help me with the presentation?
common_error.explanation: Ọ bụrụ na ndị Igbo na-egosi nkọwa dị iche iche n'okpuru okwu, ma ọ bụ naanị na nkọwa ụtọ na nkọwa ọma. N'ụdị ahịa, nkọwa na-egosi na usoro dị iche iche na usoro ụtọ, ma ọ bụ naanị na nkọwa ụtọ na nkọwa ọma.

examples.original: The company has decided to implement a new policy.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈkʌmpəni hæz dɪˈsaɪdɪd tuː ˈɪmplɪmɛnt ə njuː ˈpɒləsi/
examples.translation: Ụlọ ọrụ mere ịdị n'ọnọdụ ịmụba ọhụrụ.
examples.note: Usoro nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: We regret to inform you that your application has been unsuccessful.
examples.phonetic: /wiː rɪˈɡrɛt tʊ ɪnˈfɔːm juː ðæt jɔːr ˌæplɪˈkeɪʃən hæz biːn ˌʌnsəkˈsɛsfəl/
examples.translation: Anyị na-achọ ịgwa unu na ndoro ndoro ahu adịghị mma.
examples.note: Nkọwa nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: Would you be so kind as to sign the attached document?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː biː səʊ kaɪnd æz tə saɪn ði əˈtætʃt ˈdɒkjʊmənt/
examples.translation: Biko, bụrụ na ị nwere ike ịnye usoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Nkọwa nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: Please send me the updated version of the file.
examples.phonetic: /pliːz sɛnd miː ði ˌʌpˈdeɪtɪd ˈvɜːʃən əv ðə faɪl/
examples.translation: Biko, nyere m faịlụ ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Nkọwa na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: I'll forward you the details as soon as I get them.
examples.phonetic: /aɪl ˈfɔːwərd juː ðə ˈdiːteɪlz æz suːn æz aɪ ɡɛt ðɛm/
examples.translation: M ga-emeri gị faịlụ ndoro ndoro ndoro mgbe m na-eme ya.
examples.note: Nkọwa na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: The meeting has been postponed until next week.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ hæz biːn pəʊstˈpəʊnd ənˈtɪl nɛkst wiːk/
examples.translation: Ụgwọ ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Nkọwa na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: Wanna grab a coffee later?
examples.phonetic: /ˈwɒnə ɡræb ə ˈkɒfi ˈleɪtər/
examples.translation: Ụnọọkwu ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro?
examples.note: Nkọwa na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: I can't make it to the party tonight, sorry!
examples.phonetic: /aɪ kɑːnt meɪk ɪt tə ðə ˈpɑːti təˈnaɪt ˈsɒri/
examples.translation: Ọ dịghị m ike ịbanye n'okpuru ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Nkọwa na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

examples.original: That's a really cool idea, let's do that!
examples.phonetic: /ðæts ə ˈrɪəli kuːl aɪˈdɪə lɛts duː ðæt/
examples.translation: Ọ dị mma! M ga-eme ndoro ndoro ndoro!
examples.note: Nkọwa na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ na nke na-egosi n'ọnọdụ ụtọ.

title: Advanced Inversion and Fronting / Inversión na frontalización ndoro
bridge: Na English, nke a na-akpaghị na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a. N'igbo, anyị na-achị anya na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a. N'ụzọ dị iche, 'Rarely have I seen such beauty' na igbo bụ 'Rara vez he visto tal belleza', n'ihi na enweghi nke a na-egosi na nke a. Nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a. N'ihi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a, n'igbo, nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na nke a. Caution: you must not invert in all adverbs at the beginning, only in those that allow it.

concept_examples.text: Never have I seen such a magnificent sunset.
concept_examples.translation: A ga-emeri m anya ugwo dị iche ike.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈnɛvər hæv aɪ siːn sʌtʃ ə mæɡˈnɪfɪsənt ˈsʌnsɛt/

concept_examples.text: Only after the meeting did she realize her mistake.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.

concept_examples.text: Not only did he finish the race, but he also broke the record.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụ na nke a mere ka ha na-eme ka ha na-eme ka ha.

examples.original: Never had she felt so alone.
examples.phonetic: /ˈnɛvər hæd ʃiː fɛlt soʊ əˈloʊn/
examples.translation: A ga-emeri m anya ugwo dị iche ike.
examples.note: Usoro 'never' n'isi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a.

examples.original: Rarely do we see such dedication.
examples.phonetic: /ˈrɛrli duː wiː siː sʌtʃ ˌdɛdɪˈkeɪʃən/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.
examples.note: N'ụzọ dị iche, 'do' na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a.

examples.original: Hardly had the play started when the fire alarm went off.
examples.phonetic: /ˈhɑːrdli hæd ðə pleɪ ˈstɑːrtɪd wɛn ðə ˈfaɪər əˈlɑːrm wɛnt ɒf/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.
examples.note: Usoro 'hardly...when' na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a.

examples.original: Only by working hard can you achieve your goals.
examples.phonetic: /ˈoʊnli baɪ ˈwɜːrkɪŋ hɑːrd kæn juː əˈtʃiːv jɔːr ɡoʊlz/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ na nke a mere ka ha na-eme ka ha na-eme ka ha.
examples.note: N'ụzọ dị iche, 'only by' + gerund na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a.

examples.original: Not until midnight did the storm subside.
examples.phonetic: /nɒt ənˈtɪl ˈmɪdnaɪt dɪd ðə stɔːrm səbˈsaɪd/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.
examples.note: N'ụzọ dị iche, 'not until' na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a.

examples.original: Only when the last tree is cut down will we realize its importance.
examples.phonetic: /ˈoʊnli wɛn ðə lɑːst triː ɪz kʌt daʊn wɪl wiː ˈriːəlaɪz ɪts ɪmˈpɔːrtəns/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.

examples.original: So exhausted was she that she fell asleep instantly.
examples.phonetic: /soʊ ɪɡˈzɔːstɪd wʌz ʃiː ðæt ʃiː fɛl əˈsliːp ˈɪnstəntli/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.

examples.original: Such was the chaos that no one could hear the announcement.
examples.phonetic: /sʌtʃ wʌz ðə ˈkeɪɒs ðæt noʊ wʌn kʊd hɪər ði əˈnaʊnsmənt/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.
examples.note: 'Such' + verb + noun; nke a na-egosi na nke a na-egosi na nke a.

examples.original: That film I would never watch again.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt fɪlm aɪ wʊd ˈnɛvər wɒtʃ əˈɡɛn/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ n'oge gara aga nke ha hụrụ ike n'ime ha.
